ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier (Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 of 7 December 2016 implementing EU AMLD4/5/6) and French UBO register under Decree n° 2017-924

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of identity and address for natural-person UBO
Articles of association and beneficial ownership structure for corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and French domestic sanctions screening; UBO identification and verification required prior to incorporation filing

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: infogre.fr (aggregator of French company registries) and greffe du tribunal de commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Must be in French language using Latin alphabet; foreign names may require transliteration or adaptation per INPI rules

Offensive, discriminatory, or contrary to public policy terms

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Prohibited for French SAS; a physical address in France is mandatory

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate legal services and name search clearance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.227-1 through L.227-4 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Articles L.210-1 through L.210-10 for common incorporation rules; Articles L.123-1 et seq. for registration with the Registre National des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); final registration and Kbis issuance by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the INPI-operated RNE.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration application form under the 'formalité unique' system (immatriculation au Registre National des Entreprises), accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation (statuts), legal notice publication, and capital deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Article L.227-2 C. com.; the Articles may set share capital at €1 or such higher amount as shareholders decide. Cash contributions must be deposited on a blocked bank account or with a notary (consignation) until the company is registered. In-kind contributions must be valued by a statutory auditor unless the audit requirement is waived by unanimous shareholder consent.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders, in accordance with Articles L.227-1 to L.227-4 of the French Commercial Code, RESOLVE: (1) to approve the draft Articles of Incorporation and the initial subscription of [X] ordinary shares by each subscriber, acknowledging full payment and deposit of the subscribed capital in accordance with the capital deposit certificate; (2) to adopt the registered office at [address] within the jurisdiction of the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; (3) to appoint [Name] as President and [Name] as statutory auditor if legal thresholds are reached, with all powers granted by law and the Articles; and (4) to complete all registration formalities through the Guichet Unique and to execute all documents necessary to obtain immatriculation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the constitution notice in a licensed legal announcements gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal announcements newspaper (Support Habilité d'Annonces Légales) within the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a formal notice identifying the SAS name, share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, and first President. Submit the notice to the authorized gazette, pay the publication fee, and obtain a signed attestation of publication. This legal notice is required for commercial companies.
required_dossiers: Full text of the constitution notice
Instruction sheet from the legal announcements gazette
Payment confirmation for publication fees
Proof of identity of the legal entity/individual placing the notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette refuses the notice for incomplete information, correct the text and resubmit the same or following day; choose an alternate authorized gazette if the initial one is unavailable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare, validate, and sign the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders; notaire public if the shareholders elect notarial authenticity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure that the statuts contain all mandatory SAS clauses: corporate name, purpose including virtual performance hosting and digital ticketing, duration, share capital and share classes, registered office address, governance powers of the President, shareholders' consent rights, and decision-making procedure. Have each founder sign the statuts manually or by secure electronic signature. Notarization is optional unless real property or matrimonial law matters require it.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in French
Identity documents of all founding shareholders
French registered office address and proof of judicial/economic use of the address
List of initial directors/President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe or Guichet Unique identifies a legal defect in the clauses, amend the relevant articles, have all shareholders re-sign the affected pages or a rectification deed, and resubmit the corrected version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit the subscribed share capital into a blocked account and obtain the deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, cooperative bank, or notary acting as depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the SAS en formation, transfer the cash contributions, and request a certificate of capital deposit ('certificat de dépôt des fonds') from the depositary. If in-kind contributions are made, obtain a fair value report by a commissaire aux apports unless the requirement is waived by unanimous consent.
required_dossiers: Bank account identity form
Copy of the signed Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents of the shareholders making cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or notary queries the capital source or requires additional anti-money-laundering documentation, promptly provide the requested beneficial ownership statements and source-of-funds explanation; once cleared, obtain a replacement certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the complete incorporation file to the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by INPI, routed to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and tax authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, complete the 'immatriculation' declaration for a SAS, upload all statutory annexes, attach the capital deposit certificate and legal notice attestation, and pay the registration fee online. The dossier is electronically routed to the GREFFE, social security bodies, tax authorities, and stats authorities.
required_dossiers: Completed RNE registration application form (formalité unique)
Signed Articles of Incorporation
Legal publication attestation
Capital deposit certificate
Proof of registered office (lease, domiciliation contract, or deed of ownership)
Declaration of beneficial owner (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Identity documents of President and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique or Greffe sends a request for completion or a rejection notice, correct the deficiencies and resubmit within the statutory 15-day period; use the 'compléter la procédure' portal function to annex missing documents, then queue for renewed review by the Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Kbis certificate and complete post-registration formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Greffe has validated the dossier, check the electronic notification of registration, download the definitive 'extrait Kbis' from the RNE or Infogreffe portal, and record the SIREN/SIRET numbers. Register the company with URSSAF and the tax authorities through the automatic routing; keep the Kbis in the corporate register.
required_dossiers: Notification of completion of registration
Kbis extract issued by the Greffe
SIREN/SIRET notification
Beneficial owner registration receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains incorrect details, apply to the Greffe for rectification through the online correction process; if the Greffe fails to act within statutory deadlines, a summary application may be filed with the President of the Tribunal de Commerce.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No specific industrial licensing authority applies to pure digital virtual concert hosting; general economic competence sits with the Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) and, for labor matters, the Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — virtual performance hosting and digital ticket tokenization are not classified as a statutorily licensed activity in France. However, if the company ever organizes live performances from a physical French studio with public ticketing, the appropriate 'entrepreneur de spectacles vivants' licence of the Direction Régionale des Affaires Culturelles (DRAC) must be assessed, which is outside the present digital-only scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique, de la Biodiversité, de la Forêt, de la Mer et de la Pêche — Inspection des Installations Classées (DREAL/DRIEAT)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical installation or classified facility (ICPE) under Article L.511-1 of the Environmental Code; no Environmental Impact Assessment required for a purely digital ticketing and streaming service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A — no wastewater, VOC, or combustion emissions arise from the digital activity. All office and IT electronic waste must be taken back or collected by an approved eco-organization under Articles L.541-10-2 and R.543-1 et seq. of the Environmental Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Virtual event platform: no fire-safety certification is required because there is no 'building open to the public' (ERP). The employer must nonetheless comply with the Labour Code on electrical safety, workstation ergonomics, and display-screen health, and must draft and maintain the 'Document unique d'évaluation des risques' (DUERP). Any future physical studio or concert hall will require an ERP category L fire-authorization inspection before opening.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Relance; official portal: www.impots.gouv.fr; business formalities: www.formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned French SAS: (1) File incorporation articles via the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; (2) Upon registration at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), obtain the SIREN and SIRET numbers, which constitute the statutory TIN; (3) DGFiP automatically assigns the French intra-community VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) reflected on the Kbis extract and the corporate tax file; (4) If the entity begins taxable activities before formal issuance, apply to the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises for a provisional VAT number; (5) For a non-resident entity without permanent establishment, submit Form Cerfa 13716*03 to the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), appoint an accredited tax representative if the entity is now established outside the EU, and maintain the VAT number through the annual verification under Article 286 CGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law does not provide a 'check-the-box' election; the SAS is inherently taxable at entity level on corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés). Available elections include: (a) Fiscal integration under Article 223 A CGI for a group headed by a 95% parent; (b) VAT grouping election under Article 256 C CGI allowing established French taxable persons to form a single taxable person; (c) option under Article 209 CGI for a French company to waive the territoriality exclusion for certain foreign permanent establishments (hybrid mismatch restrictions apply under ATAD). No pass-through election exists for an SAS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for established domestic taxable persons; registration is required from the first taxable transaction. The 'franchise en base de TVA' exemption applies to established micro-businesses with annual turnover below EUR 85,000 (sales of goods) or EUR 37,500 (services), after which VAT registration is mandatory. For non-resident EU suppliers of digital services and intra-Community distance sales of goods, the union-wide distance sales threshold is EUR 10,000; below this, supplies are subject to French VAT if made to French consumers, and above it the destination-member-state tax applies via the OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing is introduced by the 2023 Finance Act and will be phased in from 1 September 2026. All VAT-registered entities must issue and receive electronic structured invoices (Factur-X, UBL, CII) through an accredited Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the public portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF). E-reporting of all transactions, including B2C sales, must be transmitted through the PPF via a certified API. France does not operate a continuous transaction control (CTC) clearance or real-time digital stamping regime; however, cash-register software used for consumer transactions must be secured and certified under NF 525 to satisfy anti-fraud requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the European Union qualify for 0% French VAT when physical export is proven by transport documents and the exporter files an electronic export declaration (DAU/DELTA-X). Digital services, including virtual concert tickets and tokenized access rights, are 'offshore services' excluded from French VAT when supplied to a business customer outside France (B2B) or to a non-EU consumer (B2C); supplies to EU consumers are subject to the place-of-residence rule, with French VAT applying only if the pan-EU EUR 10,000 threshold for TBE services has not been exceeded, and otherwise VAT is chargeable in the consumer's member state through the OSS scheme. Adequate documentation of the customer's location and status is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Customs Export Declaration (Document Administratif Unique, DAU/SAD) via DELTA-X for physical goods
Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill evidencing physical removal of goods from the EU
Commercial invoice and export contract reflecting the sale and delivery terms
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement proving payment receipt within the documentary benchmark of 180 days
For digital/offshore services: signed service agreement, customer tax identification records (e.g., EU VAT number or equivalent), and OSS/e-reporting output where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The tax administration may retrospectively claw back improperly zero-rated VAT within the statutory reassessment period (generally three calendar years after the taxable year, extended to six years for failure to file and up to ten years for fraud). Claimed export refunds lacking the required documentation are reassessed with late interest of 0.2% per month and penalties under Article 1788 A CGI: 40% for deficiencies without bad faith, and 80% for deliberate concealment or fraudulent manoeuvres. Customs infringements for false export declarations entail fines up to twice the goods' value, confiscation, and imprisonment under the Customs Code. Criminal tax fraud sanctions apply separate monetary penalties up to EUR 500,000 and five years' imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, with prudential supervision exercised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) and foreign-exchange/balance-of-payments statistical monitoring coordinated with the Direction Générale du Trésor under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full EUR convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions under European Union free-movement-of-capital rules and the CMF. There is no administrative licence, exchange registration, quantitative ceiling, or central-bank approval requirement for non-resident shareholding, foreign dividend distributions, ticket-royalty payments, or USDC conversions. Residual obligations are statistical and tax-related: (i) any cross-border transfer of EUR 10,000 or more must be reported to Banque de France through the financial institution using the Compte Rendu de Transfert de Fonds (CRTF) statistical report; and (ii) profit repatriation to non-resident shareholders is lawful after corporate approval but remains subject to French dividend withholding tax at 25% unless a tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive reduces or eliminates the rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio; the mandatory conversion ratio is effectively zero. Virtual-concert ticket revenues received via Stripe or USDC may lawfully be retained in foreign currency, credited to a French or EU-located account, or converted at negotiated market rates. The continuing requirements are: (i) correct recognition of service revenue in French GAAP accounts; (ii) full audit trail for USDC-to-EUR conversion through a licensed crypto-asset service provider; and (iii) CRTF/Banque de France statistical disclosure for every inbound or outbound transfer of EUR 10,000 or more. No Treasury surrender right exists in favour of the French State.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.legal_source_reference: CMF Articles L.151-1 et seq.; ACPR AML/CTF obligations under CMF Articles L.561-1 et seq.; European Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 on cash controls; AMF digital-asset guidance and MiCA transitional rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.practical_impact_assessment: The regime is non-restrictive for Stage 4 treasury design: the French SAS may establish USD and EUR accounts, enter into eligible FX hedging, and remit profits abroad provided statutory reporting, AML/KYC, and tax compliance are maintained. The only material constraint is documentary: the bank must support the CRTF and assist with suspicious-transaction reporting where rapid USDC/ticket flows exceed customary thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (contractually blocked sight deposit in EUR) plus operational current account and USD multi-currency account
Operational Account in EUR/USD with FX online dealing desk and cash-pooling support
Operational Account (compte courant) for EU ticket collections and treasury concentration
Operational Account and documentary-trade support (Letters of Credit, collections)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as sole treasury depository; Medium as a collection-only layer. An EU Electronic Money Institution (including Stripe European entities) may lawfully acquire, hold and settle ticket-card receipts under PSD2, but an EMI is not a credit institution and should not hold statutory capital, shareholder equity, or long-term treasury balances with the protection expected by a regulated bank. The recommended design is two-tier: Stripe serves as the payment gateway for card and virtual-ticket collections, while a Tier-1 French bank operates the capital escrow, operational liquidity, and clearing accounts. USDC must be converted into EUR through a licensed CASP before any direct credit enters a Tier-1 French bank; French banks generally do not accept USDC or other native crypto-assets directly into ordinary corporate accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law permits fully remote onboarding where identity verification is performed by compliant video-KYC or using a recognised eIDAS-qualified electronic signature certificate; there is no statutory mandate that directors appear physically at a bank branch. In practice, Tier-1 French banks with a foreign-owned SAS involved in hybrid Stripe/USDC flows will almost always require a live video interview with the legal representative and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner(s), supported by legalised identity documents and a completed AML sector questionnaire. Physical attendance is therefore not legally unavoidable but materially accelerates approval and reduces derogation requests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated foreign-controlled SAS with no domestic banking history and a hybrid EUR-card plus USDC ticket-settlement model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) K-Bis business-registry extract issued within the last three months; (ii) notarised and apostilled articles of association filed with the commercial court; (iii) Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) extract identifying every ultimate individual; (iv) legalised passports and proof-of-address for the legal representative and all UBOs; (v) signed forward contracts with artists/licensors evidencing commercial substance; (vi) a 24-month business plan with revenue mix (ticket tokens, metaverse merchandising, sponsorship) and cash-flow forecast; (vii) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for all capital injections; (viii) full AML/CFT manual addressing USDC wallet screening, OFAC/EU sanctions and transaction-monitoring thresholds; (ix) SIRET/VAT registration confirmation; and (x) an external accountant or fiduciary letter confirming virtual-event ticketing and token-redemption accounting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SAS uses only a commercial domiciliation address without an operational office in France, triggering bank concern over actual substance and country of effective management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) approved domiciliation contract with an Agréé provider under CMF Article L.123-11-2; (ii) sublease or co-working agreement for the operational hub; (iii) staffing plan and projected French payroll; (iv) minutes of shareholder/board meetings, domain and trademark registrations, and platform contracts managed from France; (v) foreign-to-French service agreements clarifying that the SAS is the contracting and revenue-recognising entity; and (vi) a written cross-border permanent-establishment and VAT analysis confirming the French supply of virtual-performance services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early-stage high-volume cross-border settlements (ticket royalties, artist advances, capital injections above EUR 100,000) before any meaningful banking relationship track record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) three-year parent-company bank references or, if newly formed, references of the shareholder(s); (ii) settlement ledgers and reconciliation reports from prior virtual or physical events; (iii) original invoices, artist/vendor contracts, and platform payout statements; (iv) audited or accountant-reviewed French GAAP or IFRS financial statements showing no round-tripping; (v) intercompany business-purpose diagram and explanation for each material payment; and (vi) written commitment to submit all Banque de France CRTF filings and to maintain an enhanced transaction-monitoring log for the first 12 months.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.recommended_banking_topology: BNP Paribas: capital escrow and treasury anchor. Société Générale: secondary operational wallet for extinction-free FX referrals. Stripe: merchant-of-record? — realistically payment facilitator for card rails. Licensed CASP: USDC conversion bridge. The SAS should avoid splitting cash across more than two Tier-1 banks due to CRTF reporting and French AML concentration rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder routes a SWIFT MT103 wire in EUR (or USD spot-converted) to the French SAS capital-escrow account held at BNP Paribas. Mandatory SWIFT narrative in field 70: 'Capital subscription / inward direct investment — increase of share capital of French limited company FR_SAS / virtual event ticketing'. The bank requires a completed recording of the CRTF for any amount equal to or exceeding EUR 10,000 in countervalue. Supporting verification: shareholder resolution approving the capital increase, a notarised/certified subscription certificate, passport copies, a signed source-of-funds letter, and a statement that funds are strictly own funds of the shareholder. Where the investor contributes USDC, the investor converts through a licensed CASP to EUR and then transfers EUR by SWIFT; direct USDC contribution to a regulated EUR account is not routinely permitted. The bank releases escrowed funds only after proof of legal completion of the share capital increase with the corporate registry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Intra-EU settlements run via SEPA Credit Transfer (standard or Instant) with same-day value. Non-EU settlements run via SWIFT MT103 priority, and any transaction of EUR 10,000 or more requires the CRTF statistical information. Artist/royalty payouts are executed as recurring MT103 payments with purpose code 'Royalties for virtual performance rights / distribution of ticket sale proceeds'. Where a foreign counterparty requires bank security, the SAS may issue an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600 or, exceptionally, a documentary collection payable at sight. FX conversion for disbursements is executed by the Tier-1 bank at spot with same-day settlement; no French forex surrender instrument is required. Final beneficiary payments in restrictive markets are routed through correspondent banks in the relevant jurisdiction, with the CRTF retained for French balance-of-payments statistics.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD outright forward (change à terme ferme) up to 12 months tenor, supported by documented ticket-royalty exposure and non-speculative hedging intent.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) allowable only for emerging-market or restricted-convertibility currencies (e.g., USD/BRL or USD/INR) where the French SAS has demonstrable contractual exposure to foreign artists or platforms; NDFs in freely convertible G10 currencies are discouraged by French bank compliance absent unusual legal constraint.
Cross-currency swap (swap de change) between USD and EUR for medium-term working-capital restructuring, hedged against ticket settlements and approved under ACPR-market-conduct rules.

Plain vanilla FX spot executed through the Tier-1 bank or licensed CASP when converting USDC-to-EUR; forward-hedging of crypto-assets is permissible only where the underlying token is economically linked to future FATCA-consistent? — NFT tickets and revenue pre-orders, and is subject to enhanced internal AML validation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_clearing_assessment: The recommended clearing pattern is: Stripe collects EUR card proceeds and guards token-sale liquidity, USDC is converted via CASP into EUR and pushed by SWIFT MT103 to BNP Paribas, BNP Paribas concentrates treasury liquidity, and outgoing artist/royalty payments leave by MT103 with CRTF reporting. This topology respects French FX-stability policy, endorses virtual-event service exports as ordinary current-account flows, and creates a clean audit trail for Banque de France statistical control.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax rate under Article 219 CGI; reduced to 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with turnover below EUR 10 million)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for SMEs on first EUR 42,500 of profit; 30% Research Tax Credit (CIR) for eligible R&D expenditure (metaverse platform and virtual performance technology); 20% Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SME prototype development; Jeune Entreprise Innovante (JEI) exemptions for R&D-intensive companies under 8 years; reduced land value and payroll levies for JEI
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward under Article 209 CGI; annual utilization capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess taxable profit; optional 1-year carryback (report en arrière) capped at EUR 1,000,000)
